title: Electrical Stimulation for Bladder Function in People With SCI
official: Improving Neurogenic Bladder in SCI Through Combined Stimulation Strategies
summary: The overall objective of this study is to evaluate the feasibility, safety, and preliminary efficacy of a home-based stimulation intervention for improvement of neurogenic lower urinary tract dysfunction in individuals with chronic incomplete spinal cord injury. This is accomplished by comparing standard of care treatment through transcutaneous tibial nerve stimulation (TTNS), an electrical stimulation of the ankle joint for improving bladder function, with transcutaneous spinal cord stimulation (TSCS) improving spinal excitability to enhance TTNS alone
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* History of Chronic traumatic SCI (\>1 year post-injury) at or above T10, AIS B-D
* History of Urinary incontinence from neurogenic bladder of SCI etiology
* Voluntarily voiding use clean intermittent catheterization (CIC) for bladder management
* Stable medication regimen (\>4 weeks)
* Able to participate in all study activities
* Able to provide informed consent
* Fluent in English

Exclusion Criteria:

* Active Urinary Tract Infection
* Indwelling catheter
* Bladder augmentation or urinary diversion
* Implanted stimulators
* Pregnancy confirmed by urine test
* Skin breakdown at electrode sites
* Have one or more treatable conditions, other than neurogenic bladder dysfunction, that may cause urinary incontinence
